thread:
michael: Heads up — after last night's package push (libnccl 2.26.1) we're seeing sporadic collective hangs on cluster-us-east2. 3 nodes with stuck allreduce, inference latency spikes, and a noticeable increase in qp timeouts. ~0.6% of requests hitting our 30s fallback. Anyone else seeing this?

ava-oncall: seeing it. Put a watch on pod-level retries and kernel logs. initial scatters show repeated 'NCCL WARN AllReduce 0: timeout' and then long stalls. grabbing dmesg.

ben: can you paste a snippet of the logs?

ava-oncall: ```
[ 1234.567890] nvidia 0000:3b:00.0: nvlink: enqueue collectives failed: NCCL WARN AllReduce 0: timeout
[ 1234.568002] kernel: watchdog: task:grpc_worker blocked for more than 120 seconds.
```

carla: we landed libnccl 2.26.1 + CUDA 12.2 kernel module updates in the midnight batch. Did we also roll any driver micropatches?

runtime-ci-bot: deploy/rollout @ 2026-03-17T00:12:07Z: libnccl=2.26.1 applied to pool-us-east2-gpu-a100 (canary: 4 nodes -> 40% of traffic).

michael: canary was 4 nodes but autoscaler pushed traffic onto them during a traffic surge. so exposure > intended.

priya: quick mitigation options: 1) pin traffic away from affected pool (route to dedicated pools in us-west) 2) rollback libnccl on those nodes 3) apply timeout circuit-breaker lower threshold to reduce end-user impact. Thoughts?

sasha: option 1 is fastest. We can change routing policy for 15m and observe. I'm concerned rollback might be tricky if kernel modules changed.

carla: rollback should be possible if we have the previous libnccl package cached. BUT if the kernel driver (nvidia.ko) was also updated, a userland libnccl rollback vs kernel mismatch could be worse. Need to confirm exact RPM/DEB artifacts.

ben: i'm seeing a pattern in metrics: collectives fail mostly for batch sizes > 8 and sequence lengths > 1024. Could be a kernel scheduling regression interacting with NCCL's transport fallback.

ava-oncall: confirmed: failures concentrated on A100 hosts with nvlink enabled. MPS usage low. suspecting a transport negotiation fallback (nvlink -> p2p) that times out under pressure.

matt: customer impact? any high-traffic customers in us-east2?

michael: two PLG customers had degraded response times; support already opened tickets. No P0s yet but SLA margin shrank for reserved tenants.

devops-bot: scheduled action: route-shift job created (#1543). shifting 20% traffic away from pool-us-east2-gpu-a100 -> us-west1-dedicated. ETA 2m.

priya: while route-shift happens, can someone check if a hotpatch is available from NVIDIA or if we should roll back the libnccl package only?

carla: reached out to driver-whitelist. The driver package stayed the same (535.54) — only libnccl userland upgraded. That makes rollback lower risk.

ben: good catch. so rollback plan: apt install libnccl2=2.25.* on affected nodes, restart runtime service, and monitor KV cache warmup. Will need to cordon nodes first.

sasha: i'll coordinate cordon/drain with oncall. We'll do a 1-node rollback as a micro-canary first.

ava-oncall: running the micro-canary: cordon node gpu-us-east2-12, drain pods, apt-get install libnccl2=2.25.8 && systemctl restart redwood-runtime.

runtime-ci-bot: job 5421: log: apt-get output: "Setting up libnccl2 (2.25.8) ..."

ava-oncall: micro-canary looks good so far — no hangs in the 10m window, collectives stable.

michael: great. proceed with staged rollback across 10 nodes with 1-min gaps. But let's keep routing changes in place until we see 30m of normal metrics.

priya: cost note — shifting traffic to us-west dedicated increases expected token cost by ~8% during the window. flagging finance/alerts.

matt: log that with customer ops so they can prepare messages if any SLOs are breached.

carla: postmortem actions to capture: 1) add stronger canary traffic shaping to avoid autoscaler overriding canary exposure 2) add kernel+lib matching checks to deploy pipeline 3) perf test cluster for large-batch collectives under nvlink stressed scenarios 4) push for an NCCL upgrade test matrix in staging.

ben: also add a temporary metric for 'collective-retries-per-request' so we can detect regressions earlier.

ava-oncall: rolling rollback executed across impacted nodes. monitoring dashboards look healthy; collective latency back to baseline.

michael: closing the immediate loop: rollback succeeded, routing remains adjusted for 30m, tickets updated. We'll follow up with a blameless postmortem tomorrow. Thanks all :thumbsup:

sasha: assigning follow-ups in the incident board. please add any logs or repro steps you found.

matt: can we also add a cost-risk column to the change approval checklist for infra libs? This would have flagged the canary exposure.

carla: noted. I'll draft the checklist update.

priya: will ping finance about the cost delta for the temporary routing.

michael: nice work. one ask: if we reattempt libnccl upgrade, let's run the nvlink large-batch stress test in a staging fleet that mirrors A100 nvlink topology.

ava-oncall: ack. creating test harness ticket with repro commands and sample traces.

runtime-ci-bot: ticket created: INF-3012: "nvlink allreduce stress + nccl 2.26 regression test"

michael: good. we'll keep this thread for immediate follow-ups. If anyone finds new failures, ping here with node IDs.
